name: Floating Island
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Add the beaten yolks and one of the whites together with the sugar
Stir into them a little of the scalded milk to prevent curdling
Remove from the fire and when cool, flavor
Pour it into a glass dish and let it become very cold
Beat up the remaining four whites of the eggs to a stiff froth
Beat into them three tablespoonfuls of sugar and two tablespoonfuls of currant jelly
Dip this over the top of the custard

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Scald the milk
2. Add the beaten yolks and one of the whites together with the sugar
3. Stir into them a little of the scalded milk to prevent curdling
4. Add all of the milk
5. Cook it the proper thickness
6. Remove from the fire and when cool, flavor
7. Pour it into a glass dish and let it become very cold
8. Beat up the remaining four whites of the eggs to a stiff froth
9. Beat into them three tablespoonfuls of sugar and two tablespoonfuls of currant jelly
10. Dip this over the top of the custard
